Movie Night v3: built, for your OK before it ships

v2 as approved, with your five tweaks, now as the code in the worktree (commit on a local branch, not on main yet). Web frames are the real class names and the app's own CSS pulled from app/globals.css; the share cards are the server's real PNGs from lib/mn-share-card-og.tsx; the iPhone frames are drawn to match RoomName.swift and RoomScreen.swift.

  • Named from the room's taste once two are seated. The host gets Shuffle and the pencil; 28 characters, own words go through the public take check. Guests and members read it.
  • No "Together we're" anywhere in Movie Night: grep -rn "Together we" app lib ios returns nothing; the check (rule 1099) fails if it comes back.
  • Faces and name, one centred groupIn the room the faces sit over the name (a long name next to five faces wrapped to two lines); on the card they sit side by side, the name on one line.
  • The card: film, year, "4.5★ from the room" once two have rated, initials with the room name, Start your own, /mn. Poster kept. No QR, no room id, initials only.
  • Guests and first-timers get one line: "Everyone picks a mood. Montage finds one film you'll all like."

Web · the room

The share card · the server's own PNGs

iPhone · drawn to match RoomName.swift

How the name is picked. The seated members' archetypes averaged, with the words in lib/group-names.ts. A room one archetype leads (over 60%) suggests "The {its own adjective} {crowd}"; any other room suggests the group name it would keep. Shuffle walks the rest: "The {crowd}", "The {own} {crowd}", "The {second's adjective} {crowd}", and "{Weekday} {crowd}" (the day the room was made). A guest counts toward the two people but has no archetype, so a host plus guests is named from the host's taste alone.

When it settles. It follows the room as people join, then stays put once the host shuffles or renames, or the host opens the moods (the name is written to the room then). Stored in the room's existing name column: no migration.
